full_text_en:
Huangmei County Zhenhua Building Materials General Company v. Huangshi Public Security Bureau — administrative appeal concerning seizure of property and infringement of enterprise property rights

Appellant (original defendant): Huangshi Public Security Bureau, Hubei Province.

Legal Representative: Zhao Zhifei, Director.

Agent ad litem: Xu Haishen, Section Chief of Legal Affairs Section, Huangshi Public Security Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Yan Xuewen, Deputy Director of the Office of the Public Security Command Center, Huangshi Public Security Bureau.

Appellee (original plaintiff): Huangmei County Zhenhua Building Materials General Company, Hubei Province.

Legal Representative: Gui Linfeng, General Manager.

The appellant, Huangshi Public Security Bureau, appealed to the Supreme People's Court against the administrative judgment (No. 4 [1994] E Xing Chu Zi) rendered by Hubei High People's Court.

In the administrative judgment rendered by the court of first instance in the case of Huangmei County Zhenhua Building Materials General Company (hereinafter referred to as Huangmei Zhenhua Company) v. Huangshi Public Security Bureau concerning the illegal seizure of property, the court found that the steel purchased by the appellee, Huangmei Zhenhua Company, using bank loans constituted lawful property of the enterprise. The act of the appellant, Huangshi Public Security Bureau, in forcibly seizing the appellee's lawful property was illegal, given that the ownership of the seized steel was clear and the relevant evidence was sufficient to demonstrate that it was unrelated to the alleged criminal suspect. During the period of seizure, the appellant exerted pressure on the appellee and, at its own office, presided over the signing of a contract between the appellee and Zhejiang Province Rui'an Production Materials Service Company (hereinafter referred to as Rui'an Shengzi Company), which had no economic contractual relationship with the appellee, thereby compelling the appellee to use its lawful property to repay debts owed by another party. This conduct infringed upon the appellee's property ownership rights, and the appellant should bear the resulting liability for compensation. In accordance with Article 54, paragraph (2), subparagraph 5, and Article 67, paragraph 1, of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the court rendered the following judgment: (1) The act of the defendant, Huangshi Public Security Bureau, in seizing 133.38 tons of steel belonging to the plaintiff, Huangmei Zhenhua Company, on April 15, 1993, is hereby set aside; (2) The defendant shall pay the plaintiff compensation for the loss of the seized steel in the amount of 357,371 yuan, and other losses in the amount of 5,100 yuan; (3) The defendant shall pay the plaintiff compensation for the interest on the loan used to purchase the seized steel.

Huangshi Public Security Bureau appealed against the judgment of first instance, raising the following main grounds: The seizure of the steel was a criminal investigative measure taken by the public security organ in handling a fraud case and therefore fell outside the scope of administrative litigation accepted by the people's courts. The appellee responded, arguing that the steel seized by Huangshi Public Security Bureau was unrelated to the alleged criminal suspect, that the purpose of the seizure was not to ascertain the facts of the crime but to "obtain some money as case-handling funds," and that the judgment of first instance was fair and should be affirmed.

The Supreme People's Court, upon trial, found the following facts: In early April 1993, the appellee, Huangmei Zhenhua Company, entered into a steel supply contract with Huangmei County Federation of Industry and Commerce Construction and Installation Company, stipulating that the appellee would supply 200 tons of steel to Huangmei Federation of Industry and Commerce Construction and Installation Company by April 24, 1993. On April 5, 1993, the appellee obtained a loan of 740,000 yuan from a credit cooperative. On April 12, it purchased 193.27 tons of steel in Ezhou City, which were loaded onto two vessels and moored at Xiongjiagou Wharf in Ezhou City awaiting transport. At around 3:00 p.m. that same day, personnel from the Criminal Investigation Detachment of the appellant, Huangshi Public Security Bureau, went to the wharf and took away Zhang Maixi, the deputy general manager employed by the appellee, who was in the process of settling accounts, and orally notified the wharf management that the two vessels' steel was not to leave the port. Upon learning of this, Gui Linfeng, the legal representative of the appellee, together with the credit officer responsible for supervising the use of the loan, rushed to Huangshi City. On April 13, they were informed by the appellant that Zhang Maixi, during his previous tenure as manager of Huangmei County Building Materials Supply and Marketing Company, had been involved in economic transactions with Rui'an Shengzi Company and other entities, had defaulted on payments, was suspected of fraud and had been placed under shelter and examination, and that the steel he had handled was being seized. Gui Linfeng immediately explained to the appellant that Huangmei Zhenhua Company was established in November 1992, and Zhang Maixi was only employed by the company in February 1993; when Zhang Maixi conducted business with Rui'an Shengzi Company and other entities, the company had not yet been established; the seized steel was purchased with the company's loan and was unrelated to the conduct for which Zhang Maixi was being investigated. Subsequently, Gui Linfeng presented to the appellant relevant supporting materials, including the bank loan certificate and invoices for the steel purchase, and requested the release of the seized steel. The appellant ignored these requests and, on April 15, 1993, issued a "List of Seized Items," transporting the entire 133.38 tons of steel from the larger vessel to Huangshi City for continued seizure. The appellee repeatedly requested release, but the appellant did not comply. During this period, Zhang Maixi's wife, hoping to secure her husband's release from shelter and examination, raised 100,000 yuan and delivered it to the appellant, which then demanded 400,000 yuan. The appellant attempted to dispose of the steel on site but failed, and repeatedly urged Rui'an Shengzi Company to purchase the seized steel to offset Zhang Maixi's debts, thereby compelling the appellee to sell the steel to Rui'an Shengzi Company to repay Zhang Maixi's obligations.

On April 29, 1993, the appellant notified Rui'an Shengzi Company to come to its office to sign a contract with the appellee. Despite the fact that the accounts of the debts between Rui'an Shengzi Company and Zhang Maixi were still unclear, the appellant presided over and participated in the signing of the "Supply and Purchase Contract" and stamped its seal at the contract certification unit. The steel price, freight liability, and remittance amount were also determined by the appellant. On May 12, 1993, Rui'an Shengzi Company remitted 240,000 yuan to the appellant's account. On the same day, the appellant released Zhang Maixi from shelter and examination. On May 20, 1993, without notifying the appellee to be present for weighing, the appellant delivered the seized steel to Rui'an Shengzi Company. Thereafter, the appellee repeatedly demanded payment from the appellant, which returned 133,000 yuan to the appellee in three installments. The remaining funds were retained by the appellant, part of which had been used by the appellant.

The Supreme People's Court held that the appellant, Huangshi Public Security Bureau, seized the steel purchased by the appellee, Huangmei Zhenhua Company, on the grounds that Zhang Maixi was suspected of fraud and was under shelter and examination, requiring a criminal investigation. This act, whether considered in fact or in law, did not constitute an investigative measure under the Criminal Procedure Law. While placing Zhang Maixi under shelter and examination, the appellant seized the appellee's property based on the same facts and reasons. The appellee, dissatisfied with the seizure, lawfully initiated an administrative action, which fell within the scope of administrative litigation accepted by the people's courts as provided in Article 11, paragraph 1, subparagraph (2), of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. The appellant was fully aware that the seized steel was neither stolen goods nor evidence that could prove the alleged suspect guilty or innocent, but rather the appellee's lawful property, unrelated to the case it was handling. Nevertheless, the appellant continued to detain the steel, refused to return it, and unilaterally manipulated the appellee into signing an economic contract with Rui'an Shengzi Company, with which it had no economic relationship whatsoever, using the appellee's lawful property to repay another party's debts. This conduct violated Article 87 of the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "[i]f, after examination, it is found that the seized articles, documents, mail, or telegrams are indeed irrelevant to the case, they shall be promptly returned to the original owner or the original post and telecommunications office," and Article 2 of the Notice of the Ministry of Public Security on Prohibiting Public Security Organs from Illegally Exceeding Their Authority to Intervene in Economic Dispute Cases, which provides that "[e]conomic disputes shall be handled by the relevant enterprises and their administrative departments, arbitration organs, and people's courts in accordance with the law; public security organs shall not intervene, and are even less permitted to under the pretext of investigating economic crimes such as fraud, use illegal means such as shelter and examination or detaining hostages to meddle in economic disputes." The economic losses thus caused to the appellee shall be compensated by the appellant in accordance with Article 67, paragraph 1, of the Administrative Procedure Law.

The facts found in the original judgment are clear, the evidence is sufficient, and the application of law is correct; the appellant's grounds for appeal are untenable. In accordance with Article 61, paragraph (1), of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

Appeal dismissed, the original judgment affirmed.

Court costs of first instance in the amount of 12,714 yuan and court costs of second instance in the amount of 12,714 yuan shall be borne by the appellant, Huangshi Public Security Bureau.
